title: The different eras of houses in the UK
paragraphs: There are many different types of houses in the UK. You may see detached, semi-detached, terraced houses or even end-of-terrace houses on a typical street. You might see mansions in more affluent parts of town, or people residing in bungalows, preferring to live a life without stairs. Quaint cottages may dot the countryside, while heading to the cities you could see any number of types of flats, including houses turned into converted flats, studios and duplexes. But one thing you will notice is that many houses come from different eras, and asking a British person about their ideal home, many of them will have a specific period property in mind.

For some, it could be Victorian houses, which are often seen with bay windows, high ceilings, stained glass doors and coloured brickwork. During the Victorian era, a huge number of houses, particularly terraced, were built in towns and cities to accommodate vast numbers of workers who were moving from more rural areas.

Georgian architecture refers to houses built during the period of 1714 and 1830 during the reigns of four British monarchs, all called George. Usually houses with this architectural style have a more symmetrical theme, both internally and externally, with a small square garden in front. For those not into older properties, new builds from the 1990s onwards offer better insulation against the cold and newer electrics. And those who prefer less maintenance could always go with the open-plan or minimalist look of the modern era.

So whether it’s high ceilings, better insulation, brickwork, bungalows or square gardens, people in Britain have a wide variety of preferences when it comes to where they live. And their ideal home may just simply be a case of what style feels like home.

vocabulary.entry: detached /dɪˈtætʃt/ adj. （房屋）独立式的
vocabulary.example: They bought a large detached house in the suburbs.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在郊区买了一栋宽敞的独立式房屋。

vocabulary.entry: semi-detached /ˌsemi dɪˈtætʃt/ adj. （房屋）半独立式的
vocabulary.example: The semi-detached villa shares a wall with the neighbouring house.
vocabulary.translation: 这栋半独立式别墅和隔壁房子共用一堵墙。

vocabulary.entry: terraced /ˈterəst/ adj. （房屋）联排式的
vocabulary.example: Terraced houses are common in the city centre.
vocabulary.translation: 联排房屋在市中心很常见。

vocabulary.entry: end-of-terrace /ˌend əv ˈterəs/ adj. 联排端头房的
vocabulary.example: The end-of-terrace house has windows on three sides.
vocabulary.translation: 这套联排端头房三面都有窗户。

vocabulary.entry: mansion /ˈmænʃn/ n. 豪宅；公馆
vocabulary.example: A historic mansion stands at the top of the hill.
vocabulary.translation: 一座历史悠久的豪宅坐落在山顶。

vocabulary.entry: affluent /ˈæfluənt/ adj. 富裕的；富足的
vocabulary.example: The hotel is located in an affluent neighbourhood.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店位于一个富裕的街区。

vocabulary.entry: reside /rɪˈzaɪd/ v. 居住；定居
vocabulary.example: She resides in a quiet village in the countryside.
vocabulary.translation: 她住在乡下一个宁静的村庄里。

vocabulary.entry: bungalow /ˈbʌŋɡələʊ/ n. 平房；单层住宅
vocabulary.example: The elderly couple moved into a bungalow to avoid climbing stairs.
vocabulary.translation: 这对老年夫妇搬进了一间平房，这样就不用爬楼梯了。

vocabulary.entry: quaint /kweɪnt/ adj. 古雅的；别致的
vocabulary.example: We stayed in a quaint cottage during our holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 我们度假时住在一间古雅的小屋里。

vocabulary.entry: cottage /ˈkɒtɪdʒ/ n. （乡村）小屋；村舍
vocabulary.example: The cottage is surrounded by a small garden with roses.
vocabulary.translation: 这间村舍被一个种满玫瑰的小花园环绕着。

vocabulary.entry: dot /dɒt/ v. 散布；点缀
vocabulary.example: Small villages dot the landscape in this region.
vocabulary.translation: 小村庄点缀着这个地区的风景。

vocabulary.entry: converted flat /kənˈvɜːtɪd flæt/ 改建公寓
vocabulary.example: The old factory has been turned into a stylish converted flat.
vocabulary.translation: 这座旧工厂被改造成了一套时髦的改建公寓。

vocabulary.entry: studio /ˈstjuːdiəʊ/ n. 单身公寓；一室公寓
vocabulary.example: The studio is ideal for a single person working in the city.
vocabulary.translation: 这套单身公寓很适合在城里工作的单身人士。

vocabulary.entry: duplex /ˈdjuːpleks/ n. 复式公寓
vocabulary.example: The duplex has two floors connected by an internal staircase.
vocabulary.translation: 这套复式公寓有两层，由室内楼梯连接。

vocabulary.entry: era /ˈɪərə/ n. 时代；年代
vocabulary.example: This building dates back to the Victorian era.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑可以追溯到维多利亚时代。

vocabulary.entry: period property /ˈpɪəriəd ˈprɒpəti/ 年代房产
vocabulary.example: Many buyers are willing to pay more for a well-preserved period property.
vocabulary.translation: 许多买家愿意为保存完好的年代房产支付更高的价格。

vocabulary.entry: Victorian /vɪkˈtɔːriən/ adj. 维多利亚时代的
vocabulary.example: The street is lined with Victorian houses with beautiful facades.
vocabulary.translation: 这条街上排列着许多立面精美的维多利亚式房屋。

vocabulary.entry: bay window /beɪ ˈwɪndəʊ/ 凸窗
vocabulary.example: She likes to sit by the bay window and read books on rainy days.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢下雨天坐在凸窗边看书。

vocabulary.entry: stained glass door /steɪnd ɡlɑːs dɔː(r)/ 彩色玻璃门
vocabulary.example: The stained glass door adds a touch of elegance to the entrance.
vocabulary.translation: 这扇彩色玻璃门给入口处增添了一丝优雅。

vocabulary.entry: brickwork /ˈbrɪkwɜːk/ n. 砌砖工程；砖墙
vocabulary.example: The brickwork of the old church has been carefully restored.
vocabulary.translation: 这座老教堂的砖墙已经被精心修复。

vocabulary.entry: accommodate /əˈkɒmədeɪt/ v. 容纳；为……提供住处
vocabulary.example: The new hostel can accommodate up to 100 guests.
vocabulary.translation: 这家新青年旅社最多可容纳100位客人。

vocabulary.entry: Georgian architecture /ˈdʒɔːdʒən ˈɑːkɪtektʃə(r)/ 乔治亚式建筑
vocabulary.example: Georgian architecture is known for its symmetrical design.
vocabulary.translation: 乔治亚式建筑以其对称的设计而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: reign /reɪn/ n. 统治期；在位时期
vocabulary.example: The castle was built during the reign of King Henry VIII.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城堡建于亨利八世统治时期。

vocabulary.entry: monarch /ˈmɒnək/ n. 君主；帝王
vocabulary.example: The monarch attended the opening ceremony of the new hospital.
vocabulary.translation: 君主出席了这家新医院的落成典礼。

vocabulary.entry: symmetrical /sɪˈmetrɪkl/ adj. 对称的
vocabulary.example: The building has a symmetrical facade with two large windows on each side.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑的立面是对称的，每侧都有两扇大窗户。

vocabulary.entry: insulation /ˌɪnsjuˈleɪʃn/ n. 隔热；保温层
vocabulary.example: The house has good insulation, so it stays warm in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 这栋房子的隔热效果很好，冬天很暖和。

vocabulary.entry: electrics /ɪˈlektrɪks/ n. 电气设备；电路系统
vocabulary.example: We need to check the electrics before moving into the new house.
vocabulary.translation: 搬入新房前，我们需要检查一下电路系统。

vocabulary.entry: maintenance /ˈmeɪntənəns/ n. 维护；保养
vocabulary.example: The small cottage requires very little maintenance.
vocabulary.translation: 这间小村舍几乎不需要什么维护。

vocabulary.entry: open-plan /ˈəʊpən plæn/ adj. （空间）开放式的
vocabulary.example: The open-plan kitchen and living room is perfect for entertaining guests.
vocabulary.translation: 开放式的厨房和客厅非常适合招待客人。

vocabulary.entry: minimalist /ˈmɪnɪməlɪst/ adj. 极简主义的
vocabulary.example: She prefers a minimalist interior design with few decorations.
vocabulary.translation: 她更喜欢装饰很少的极简主义室内设计。

sentences.english: There are many different types of houses in the UK.
sentences.chinese: 英国的房屋类型丰富多样。

sentences.english: You may see detached, semi-detached, terraced houses or even end-of-terrace houses on a typical street.
sentences.chinese: 在一条普通的街道上，你可能会看到独栋别墅、双拼别墅、连排别墅，甚至是排屋端头房。

sentences.english: You might see mansions in more affluent parts of town, or people residing in bungalows, preferring to live a life without stairs.
sentences.chinese: 在城镇的富人区，你会见到各式豪宅；也有人选择住在平房里，就为了省去爬楼梯的麻烦。

sentences.english: Quaint cottages may dot the countryside, while heading to the cities you could see any number of types of flats, including houses turned into converted flats, studios and duplexes.
sentences.chinese: 古雅别致的乡村小屋星罗棋布地点缀着乡间田野，而在城市里，公寓的种类更是五花八门，包括由民宅改建而成的公寓、单身公寓以及复式公寓。

sentences.english: But one thing you will notice is that many houses come from different eras, and asking a British person about their ideal home, many of them will have a specific period property in mind.
sentences.chinese: 不过有一点你肯定会发现，英国的许多房屋都来自不同的历史时期，要是问起英国人心中的理想居所，很多人都会想到某一种特定的老式建筑。

sentences.english: For some, it could be Victorian houses, which are often seen with bay windows, high ceilings, stained glass doors and coloured brickwork.
sentences.chinese: 对有些人来说，理想居所就是维多利亚时期的房子。这类房子通常带有凸窗、高挑的天花板、彩色玻璃门和彩色砖石外墙。

sentences.english: During the Victorian era, a huge number of houses, particularly terraced, were built in towns and cities to accommodate vast numbers of workers who were moving from more rural areas.
sentences.chinese: 维多利亚时代，城镇里建造了大量房屋，尤其是连排别墅，目的是为了容纳大批从乡村迁居而来的务工人员。

sentences.english: Georgian architecture refers to houses built during the period of 1714 and 1830 during the reigns of four British monarchs, all called George.
sentences.chinese: 乔治王朝风格建筑指的是1714年至1830年间建造的房屋，这一时期正值英国四位名为乔治的君主相继统治。

sentences.english: Usually houses with this architectural style have a more symmetrical theme, both internally and externally, with a small square garden in front.
sentences.chinese: 这类风格的房屋通常内外设计都更讲究对称，门前还配有一方小巧的庭院。

sentences.english: For those not into older properties, new builds from the 1990s onwards offer better insulation against the cold and newer electrics.
sentences.chinese: 对于不喜欢老式建筑的人而言，20世纪90年代以后建成的新房有着更好的防寒保温效果和更新的电路系统。

sentences.english: And those who prefer less maintenance could always go with the open-plan or minimalist look of the modern era.
sentences.chinese: 而那些偏爱少费心打理房屋的人，则可以选择现代风格的开放式或极简主义住宅。

sentences.english: So whether it’s high ceilings, better insulation, brickwork, bungalows or square gardens, people in Britain have a wide variety of preferences when it comes to where they live.
sentences.chinese: 所以，不管是偏爱高挑的天花板、良好的保温效果、砖石外墙、平房还是方形庭院，英国人对于居所的喜好可谓各不相同。

sentences.english: And their ideal home may just simply be a case of what style feels like home.
sentences.chinese: 而他们心中的理想之家，说到底不过是一种能让人找到家的归属感的建筑风格罢了。
